messages:
oliver: Hey team — customer says they can still call the API fine (token generation, embeddings) but the Console shows 403 on Project Settings and Roles. They had a SAML->SCIM group rename yesterday. Filing details below from their screenshots and my quick checks.

amelia: do we know which project and which exact action returned 403? UI, API, or both?

oliver: UI only for project-level settings: trying to open Settings -> Members returns a 403 modal. They can list org members via API `GET /v1/orgs/:org_id/members` (200) but `GET /v1/projects/:project_id/members` from the Console session errors with 403 in the UI flow. They provided the Console network log: `GET /v1/projects/px-abc123/members 403 {"error":"permission denied"}`.

amelia: hmm. SCIM rename could have left role mapping intact at the org scope but not at project scope if we cache group->project bindings. Can you confirm if the user's principal has an org role but no project membership?

oliver: They say the user used to be in group `acme-engineers` which mapped to Org role `Developer` and Project role `Writer`. SCIM rename changed group to `acme-eng`. SCIM listing via Admin Console shows `acme-eng` mapped to Developer at org-level. Project listing in our admin DB shows no binding for `acme-eng` — previously had `acme-engineers -> Writer` binding.

devin: That sounds like a stale project-binding cache. I remember we have a per-org cached mapping keyed by group display name (ugh). If SCIM payload changed the displayName we lose the project binding until a resync or cache eviction.

kai: quick mitigation: can you ask them to trigger a manual role sync from their IdP (if supported) or we can run a server-side resync for that org. I can run an immediate resync for acme corp.

oliver: I'll ask if they can do a re-sync; meanwhile can you run the server-side job, kai? Customer is blocked from inviting a new collaborator. This is blocking their deployment pipeline.

kai: on it. running `support-bot: run job iam:resync --org acme-corp --force` now.

support-bot: job queued: iam:resync  id=job-9921  queued by kai

support-bot: job started: iam:resync  id=job-9921

support-bot: job completed: iam:resync  id=job-9921  duration=17s  result=success  note="refreshed 1 group bindings, 0 new bindings"

oliver: asked the customer to hard-refresh Console (incognito) and try again. They confirm: still 403 for Project Settings -> Members. API project members `GET /v1/projects/:id/members` still 403 when called from the Console session bearer, but works when using their admin personal token.

amelia: that suggests the API token used by the Console (session cookie->short token) isn't getting project role attached. Could be missing claim in the session token issued after the SCIM change. Check auth logs for token issuance for that user.

kai: pulled the auth trace: session token created at 2026-07-12T14:03:12Z with claims: `{"sub":"u-324","org":"org-acme","roles":["Developer"],"projects":[]}` — projects array empty. The old tokens used to include `"projects":["px-abc123"]`. So at issuance time the backend didn't populate project memberships.

devin: why would project memberships be missing? We populate them when user session is created by looking up group->project bindings using group identifiers in SCIM. If the SCIM group rename produced a new external_id or changed the displayName mapping key, the lookup fails. We need to either (a) make the lookup resilient to displayName changes, mapping by external_id instead, or (b) run a one-off remap for historical bindings.

oliver: Customer asks for a workaround now — they want their user to have console access immediately. Is there a safe temporary fix we can apply server-side?

kai: yes: I can re-create the project binding for the new group name to point to px-abc123. Running `db:insert project_bindings (org,group_identifier,project,role) values ("org-acme","scim:acme-eng:ext-456","px-abc123","Writer")` — doing it in a migration-like safe path so it survives resync. Will annotate with ticket id.

support-bot: migration started: db:migrate:patch id=mig-2026-iam-77

support-bot: migration completed: db:migrate:patch id=mig-2026-iam-77  status=ok

kai: binding created. Ask user to sign out and sign back in so session gets rebuilt.

oliver: customer did sign-out/sign-in. Confirmed they can now open Project Settings and invite members. No more 403. They also verified their CLI personal token still works.

amelia: root cause summary: SCIM group rename changed the group identifier/displayName that our legacy project-binding lookup keyed on; binding existed for old name but lookup failed for new name, so newly minted session tokens did not include project membership claim and UI requests returned 403.

devin: action items:
- follow-up PR to switch project-binding lookups to prefer SCIM external_id and fall back to displayName for older bindings (assigned to dev).
- add a background job to reconcile group renames to existing bindings and emit an alert when SCIM group id/displayName changes (assigned to eng-infra).
- add instrumentation to auth token issuance to log when project membership is empty for previously-member users (assigned to devex).

kai: filed follow-up task: IAM-3487 (reconcile scim group renames) and IAM-3488 (auth token instrumentation). tagging devin & amelia.

oliver: customer asked for a short write-up to include in their postmortem. I added incident ID INC-2026-4562 and the migration note.

amelia: nice work. marking this resolved for now, will track the follow-ups. :thumbsup:

oliver: closing thread — will reopen if customer reports recurrence.
